# The kit on OpenCode 2.x

`dist/opencode/` is generated by `devil export opencode` from the kit's Claude-format
sources. Never edit it: `bash tools/export.sh --check opencode` regenerates into a temp
directory and fails on any difference, and CI runs it.

Verified against OpenCode **2.0.18** on 2026-09-30. Every claim below is in
`doc/HARNESSES.md`, section "OpenCode, measured for X1", with the command that produced
it and the output it produced. Nothing here is inferred from documentation alone.

## Install

`$KIT` below is the absolute path of the kit checkout: the directory holding `bin/`,
`hooks/`, `rules/` and `skills/`. In a worktree it is the worktree, not the main
checkout, because the bridge refuses to use the one variable that resolves to the main
checkout.

Three symlinks, one config key. Nothing is copied, so exporting in the kit is visible in
every host wired this way on the next run.

```sh
KIT=/path/to/claude-deal-with-the-devil
HOST=/path/to/your/project
mkdir -p "$HOST/.opencode/plugins"
ln -sfn "$KIT/dist/opencode/agents"          "$HOST/.opencode/agents"
ln -sfn "$KIT/dist/opencode/commands"        "$HOST/.opencode/commands"
ln -sfn "$KIT/dist/opencode/plugins/devil.js" "$HOST/.opencode/plugins/devil.js"
```

Then merge this into the host's `opencode.json` (or `opencode.jsonc`):

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "skills": ["/absolute/path/to/kit/skills"]
}
```

The `skills` entry is what makes the kit's skills load. Do not also link the kit's
`skills/` to the host's `.claude/skills`: OpenCode would read the same IDs twice, and
Claude Code in the same host would load them as unnamespaced project skills on top of
the `devil` plugin's own copies.

The three symlinks above assume the host has no `.opencode/agents` or
`.opencode/commands` of its own. When it has, link each generated file into the host's
directory instead of replacing the directory, and let a host file of the same name win.

The committed `opencode.json` in this directory is the same fragment with `@KIT_ROOT@`
where the absolute path goes. It is a fragment to merge, never a file to copy over the
host's.

### What the setup stage has to write

The setup tool is a later slice and is not in this tree yet, so nothing here names its
file. These are the paths and the key it will have to write, and this table is the
contract between the two slices.

| Path in the host | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `.opencode/agents` | symlink to `<kit>/dist/opencode/agents` | the subagents |
| `.opencode/commands` | symlink to `<kit>/dist/opencode/commands` | the commands and workflows |
| `.opencode/plugins/devil.js` | symlink to `<kit>/dist/opencode/plugins/devil.js` | the hook bridge |
| `opencode.json` | merge in `{"skills": ["<kit>/skills"]}` | loads the skills |
| `AGENTS.md` | do not touch | the host owns it, and the bridge already injects the rules |

An existing `opencode.json` is merged, never replaced: the key to write is `skills`, and
every other key in the host's file stays as it is.

## What works

| Kit asset | On OpenCode | How |
|---|---|---|
| Skills | full | the `skills` config key; `name` and `description` are read, the ID comes from the path |
| Agents | full | `.opencode/agents/*.md` with `mode: subagent` and a `permissions` list |
| Tool restrictions | full | a Claude `tools:` list becomes a V2 `permissions` list: a deny-all base rule, then one allow per granted action |
| Commands | full, one gap | `.opencode/commands/*.md`, `$ARGUMENTS` kept, `/devil:<name>` rewritten to the `/<name>` V2 registers |
| Deny a tool call | full | the bridge sets `effect: "deny"` in `ctx.permission.hook("evaluate")`; the reason reaches the model verbatim |
| Ask on the irreversible | full | the same hook with `effect: "ask"`. It prompts in a session and auto-approves under `opencode run --auto`, which is what `--auto` means. A segmented command has no ask channel, so there it arrives as a refusal |
| Post-edit gates | full | `tool.execute.after` on write, edit and patch; the verdict is injected on the next model call |
| Session briefing | full | `hooks.py` `SessionStart` once per session, injected through `session.context` |
| Always-on rules | full | injected as system text by the bridge, from the kit's own `rules/*.md` |
| `bin/devil` on the agent's PATH | full | `shell.create.before` prepends `<kit>/bin`, so `command -v devil` resolves |

No `AGENTS.md` is generated. V2 reads `AGENTS.md` and nothing else, but the bridge already
delivers the same text, so a generated file would be a second copy a host might load on top
of the injection and pay for twice. A host that cannot load the plugin at all can build the
file itself from the kit's rules:

```sh
{ echo '# Always-on rules'; for f in "$KIT"/rules/*.md; do cat "$f"; done; } >"$HOST/AGENTS.md"
```

## What is degraded

| Gap | Consequence | Why it cannot be fixed here |
|---|---|---|
| No `paths:` scoping | the 7 `stage: rule` skills (`refactor-c`, `refactor-go`, `refactor-rust`, `refactor-typescript`, `refactor-shell`, `api-convention`, `script-library`) load whenever the model picks them, not only on a matching file | V2 skill frontmatter has no glob field. The nearest equivalent is an `AGENTS.md` inside the subtree, which loads when the agent reads a file under it |
| No `!` shell injection under `opencode run` | a command template's shell block reaches the model as prompt text | measured: `opencode run` neither expands a template nor runs the block. It is a TUI command-evaluation feature |
| No plugin path in `opencode.json` | `plugins: ["<path>"]` is documented and does not work in 2.0.18 | measured four ways: a bare directory of `.js` files, and a directory with a `package.json`; absolute and relative paths; with and without `--standalone`. The symlink is the route that works |
| A plugin cannot add a skill | nothing is registered from the bridge, so the `skills` key or the symlink is mandatory | `ctx.skill.transform` resolves without error and `editor.add` never reaches the registry |
| `CLAUDE.md` is not read | a host's Claude Code instructions are invisible here | V2 recognises `AGENTS.md` only |
| The `instructions` config key is dead | it parses and adds nothing | the V2 config schema accepts the array; V2 does not resolve its files, globs or URLs |
| A compound shell command is checked in two pieces | a denied pattern after a `;`, `&&`, `\|` or a newline needs the tool hook to catch it, and the check is a refusal rather than a prompt | measured: `command -v devil; echo git push --force origin main` reached the permission hook as `command -v devil` and the rest ran. The bridge re-checks a segmented command whole. A separator built at runtime is invisible to it, exactly as it is to `risk.py` |
| Model names do not port | the kit's agents carry `model: opus` and `sonnet`, which mean nothing here | V2 wants `provider/model#variant`, and the right provider is the host's choice, so it is left to the host config |
| Only two of the two shell forms | V2 has no `bash` action | a shell command is the `shell` action and the `shell` tool. The generated agents say `shell`; the source kit says `Bash` |

## What is not supported

- `templates/mcp.json`. V2 reads `mcp.servers` in config, or a plugin
  `ctx.mcp.transform`. Not generated here; a host declares its own.
- `hooks/hooks.json` file for file. V2 has no event names and no matcher. The bridge
  implements the four events that have a V2 equivalent, and the other twenty-nine are
  unreachable. On Claude Code all of them fire; here only enforcement, the post-edit
  gate, the session briefing and the PATH exist.
- `PreCompact`. V2 has a `session.hook("compaction")` event, but it takes the messages
  being summarized and a replacement summary, not advice for the next model call, so
  the kit's "preserve these facts" note has nowhere to go.
- Namespaced command names. V2 registers `/<name>` at the top level with no namespace, so
  a host command of the same name wins. The generated descriptions say `/<name>`, which is
  what is actually registered.
- A plugin that registers agents. `ctx.agent.transform` can update and remove, never add,
  so the agents are files under `.opencode/agents/` and the symlink is not optional.
- Attribution of a commit, a push or a deploy, which stays a human action whatever the
  harness. The bridge enforces only what `hooks/scripts/risk.py` enforces.

## Verifying an install

```sh
DEVIL_BRIDGE_DEBUG=/tmp/bridge.log opencode run --standalone --auto \
  -m 'PROVIDER/MODEL' --agent build \
  "list the skills you can see, then run 'command -v devil', then try 'git push --force origin main'"
```

Three answers in order: the kit's skills are advertised, `devil` resolves under the kit's
`bin/`, and the force-push is refused with the kit's reason. `DEVIL_BRIDGE_DEBUG` writes one
line per hook the bridge serves, which is the only way to see what a fail-open bridge was
actually shown.
